requirement:
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.

A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`. All are in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` under `mod[tests]`.

- **Scope of functions (methods, test functions, helpers):** `fn[methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported]` uses an impl method, a `#[test]` function and a helper inside `mod tests`. It asserts that each appears as `#<selector>: zero execution`.
- **Default trait methods:** `fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` asserts that `#trait[T]/fn[body]: zero execution` is reported.
- **Declarations without bodies create no obligation:**
  - The same test asserts that `fn[declaration]` is absent from the report.
  - It also asserts that the inventory reports a trait containing only a declaration as having no obligations.
  - It checks that macro invocations and derives create no function obligations.
  - `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` shows a file with only a declaration reported as `no executable obligations — pass`.
- **Nested functions and closures:** `fn[overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent]` checks that a nested function or closure does not hide an unexecuted parent, in both directions.
- **First-party and vendor boundary:** `fn[post_suite_scope_excludes_root_vendor_but_includes_source_vendor]` asserts that `src/vendor/first_party.rs` is included and the check fails because of it. It also asserts that `- vendor/foreign.rs` is absent. The report writes file lines as `- {file}: ...` and error lines as `- {file}:...`, so this negative assertion would catch a root-`vendor` file if one were wrongly included.
- **Parse failures fail the check:** `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` writes malformed Rust (`fn malformed(`). It asserts that `passed` is false and that the text contains "cannot parse rust source".
- **Discovery failures fail the check:** the discovery test writes an invalid `.gitignore` (`[z-a]`). It asserts that `passed` is false and that the text contains "cannot discover reference sources".
- **Unmeasurable functions reported as not measured:**
  - The default-trait test asserts that the `#[cfg(any())]` function is reported as `#fn[excluded]: not measured`.
  - The unmeasured-files test asserts `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` and `#fn[missing]: not measured` when function attribution is empty.
- **Build-configuration exclusions needing exception evidence:** the cfg-excluded function is shown as an unmet obligation, not silently dropped. The exception mechanics belong to `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, which this requirement only cites, so they are not assessed here.

All of these tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligation.

The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
